# package mpdo

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-canopen/mpdo"
```

Package mpdo implements CANopen multiplexed PDOs (MPDOs, CiA 301 7.2.2.4 and the object scanner and dispatcher lists 0x1FA0..0x1FFF): PDOs that carry one value of up to 4 bytes together with the object it belongs to, so that one COB-ID can transport many objects.

#### Frame {#hdr-Frame}

An MPDO is always 8 bytes ([Message](#type-message)):

	byte 0     bit 7: address mode (0 SAM, 1 DAM); bits 0..6: node-ID
	bytes 1..2 object index (little-endian)
	byte 3     object sub-index
	bytes 4..7 the value, padded with zeros

In destination address mode (DAM) the node-ID is the consumer's (0: all consumers) and the object is the consumer's object the value is written to. In source address mode (SAM) the node-ID is the producer's and the object is the producer's own; each consumer finds the local object in its object dispatcher list.

#### Configuration {#hdr-Configuration}

A PDO is an MPDO when sub-index 00h of its mapping parameter is 0xFE (MappingSAM) or 0xFF (MappingDAM), with an event-driven transmission type (254, 255). The COB-ID, transmission type and inhibit time are the usual communication parameters (0x1400.., 0x1800..). As in Lely CANopen (lely-core src/co/rpdo.c, pdo.c co\_mpdo\_dn), the value has the same meaning on the receive side: an RPDO with 0xFE consumes SAM-MPDOs, one with 0xFF DAM-MPDOs, and an MPDO of the other mode is ignored.

A SAM producer may only send objects listed in its object scanner list (0x1FA0..0x1FCF, [ScannerEntry](#type-scannerentry)); a SAM consumer writes only values that match an entry of its object dispatcher list (0x1FD0..0x1FFF, [DispatcherEntry](#type-dispatcherentry)). Both entries describe a block of consecutive sub-indices: block size n covers sub-index s..s+n-1 (0 counts as 1, as Lely does), and a dispatcher entry maps the k-th sub-index of the producer's block to the k-th of the local block.

#### Services {#hdr-Services}

[Producer](#type-producer) (a TPDO whose mapping sub 00h is 0xFE or 0xFF) sends DAM-MPDOs ([Producer.SendDAM](#func-producer-senddam)) or SAM-MPDOs ([Producer.Send](#func-producer-send), checked against the scanner list; the value is read with a remote read so read hooks apply). [Consumer](#type-consumer) (an RPDO whose mapping sub 00h is 0xFE or 0xFF) writes received values with remote writes ([od.Dictionary.Write](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen/od#Dictionary.Write)), so access rights, limits, write hooks and watchers apply; the local object must exist, be PDO-mappable and writable. The value written has the object's data type size when that is at most 4 bytes, otherwise 4 bytes (Lely co\_mpdo\_dn): a larger fixed-size object is refused by the dictionary.

Both follow their parameters in the dictionary, and send or receive only while enabled ([Producer.SetEnabled](#func-producer-setenabled), NMT operational) and active (COB-ID valid, MPDO mapping, event-driven type).

#### Errors and emergencies {#hdr-Errors_and_emergencies}

The consumer reports two emergencies through [WithErrorHandler](#func-witherrorhandler) as pdo.ErrorEvent values (so a node can feed them to the same handler as its RPDOs):

  - 0x8230 (EMCYDAMNoObject, CiA 301 table 21 "DAM MPDO not processed, destination object not available"; Wireshark's packet-canopen.c lists the same text): a DAM-MPDO addressed to this node (or to all) names an object or sub-index the dictionary lacks. Lely raises it in the same case (co\_rpdo\_read\_frame).
  - 0x8210 (pdo.EMCYPDOLength): an MPDO shorter than 8 bytes, as Lely reports a PDO length error for it.

Each is reported once when it appears and once when it is resolved: 0x8230 by the next DAM-MPDO for this node that is written, 0x8210 by the next MPDO of 8 bytes. (The resolution rule is this package's choice; Lely reports every occurrence.) Other refusals — an object that is not mappable or not writable, a write the dictionary refuses, a SAM-MPDO without a dispatcher entry, a DAM-MPDO for another node — are ignored and counted in [ConsumerStats](#type-consumerstats), as in Lely. Frames longer than 8 bytes (CAN FD) are used up to their 8th byte, as Lely does.

#### Reconfiguration rules {#hdr-Reconfiguration_rules}

[NewProducer](#func-newproducer) and [NewConsumer](#func-newconsumer) install write hooks on their PDO's mapping and communication parameters (see [ProtectPDO](#func-protectpdo)); [ProtectLists](#func-protectlists) installs the hooks that validate scanner and dispatcher entries. Both complement pdo.Protect, which a node installs on every PDO.

#### Sources {#hdr-Sources}

Frame layout, SAM/DAM semantics, the 0xFE/0xFF mapping values, the scanner entry layout (bits 0..7 sub-index, 8..23 index, 24..31 block size), the block matching and dispatch arithmetic, the value size rule and the emergencies follow Lely CANopen (lely-core include/lely/co/pdo.h, src/co/pdo.c co\_dev\_chk\_sam\_mpdo, co\_dev\_map\_sam\_mpdo, co\_sam\_mpdo\_up, co\_mpdo\_dn; src/co/tpdo.c co\_dam\_mpdo\_event, co\_sam\_mpdo\_event; src/co/rpdo.c). The dispatcher entry layout (bits 0..7 producer node-ID, 8..15 producer sub-index, 16..31 producer index, 32..39 local sub-index, 40..55 local index, 56..63 block size) is the one documented by embedded-communication.com ("CANopen MPDO - An introduction") and used by Lely for every field but the block size, which Lely reads at bit 54 (apparently a slip: bits 54..55 belong to the local index); this package uses bits 56..63. The object ranges 0x1FA0..0x1FCF and 0x1FD0..0x1FFF are those of CiA 301 (the CiA CANopen poster, CANopenNode doc/objectDictionary.md, Wireshark). "Event-driven only" is CiA 301 as quoted by embedded-communication.com; Lely likewise sends nothing for a synchronous MPDO.

### func ProtectLists

```go
func ProtectLists(d *od.Dictionary) (unprotect func())
```

ProtectLists installs write hooks on every object scanner and dispatcher list of d that validate remote writes of entries ([ScannerEntry.Validate](#func-scannerentry-validate), [DispatcherEntry.Validate](#func-dispatcherentry-validate); a scanner entry wider than 32 bits, possible only in a list not built by [NewScannerList](#func-newscannerlist), is refused with [canopen.AbortInvalidValue](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortInvalidValue)); the number of entries (sub-index 00h) is bounded by the object's limits. Local writes are not checked. The returned function removes the hooks (later calls do nothing). Lists added to d afterwards are not covered.

### func ProtectPDO

```go
func ProtectPDO(d *od.Dictionary, transmit bool, n int) (unprotect func(), err error)
```

ProtectPDO installs write hooks on TPDO (transmit) or RPDO n of d with the MPDO rules, which complement those of pdo.Protect:

  - mapping sub-index 00h: setting 0xFE or 0xFF while the COB-ID is valid and the value differs, or while the transmission type is not event-driven: [canopen.AbortUnsupported](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortUnsupported) and [canopen.AbortInvalidValue](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortInvalidValue) respectively; changing it away from 0xFE/0xFF while the COB-ID is valid: [canopen.AbortUnsupported](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortUnsupported).
  - mapping sub-indices 01h..: any write while sub 00h is 0xFE or 0xFF: [canopen.AbortUnsupported](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortUnsupported) (Lely: entries change only while sub 00h is 0).
  - communication sub-index 02h: a type other than 254/255 while the PDO is an MPDO: [canopen.AbortInvalidValue](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortInvalidValue) (MPDOs are event-driven only).

Note that pdo.Protect itself (v0.2.0) refuses 0xFE/0xFF in sub 00h with [canopen.AbortPDOLength](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortPDOLength); where both are installed, a PDO can only be made an MPDO by a local write until pdo accepts the two values. The returned function removes the hooks (later calls do nothing).

### func Scanned

```go
func Scanned(d *od.Dictionary, index uint16, sub uint8) bool
```

Scanned reports whether the object scanner lists of d allow a SAM-MPDO of index:sub (Lely co\_dev\_chk\_sam\_mpdo). An entry value wider than 32 bits allows nothing.

## Types

### type Consumer

```go
type Consumer struct {

	// COB-ID subscribed to (valid when sub != nil)
	// 0x8210 active
	// 0x8230 active

}
```

Consumer is an MPDO consumer: RPDO n of a dictionary whose mapping sub-index 00h is 0xFE (it consumes SAM-MPDOs, routed through the object dispatcher lists) or 0xFF (it consumes DAM-MPDOs addressed to the dictionary's node-ID or to all nodes). It follows changes of its parameters and writes values with remote writes (see the package documentation for the checks and the emergencies).

#### func NewConsumer

```go
func NewConsumer(bus canopen.Bus, d *od.Dictionary, n int, opts ...Option) (*Consumer, error)
```

NewConsumer returns the MPDO consumer of RPDO n (1..512) of d. It installs the MPDO reconfiguration rules ([ProtectPDO](#func-protectpdo)) and does nothing on the bus. Call Start, and SetEnabled(true) when the node is NMT operational.

```go

A second Start fails with [canopen.ErrBusy](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#ErrBusy), a Start after Close with [canopen.ErrClosed](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#ErrClosed).

### type DispatcherEntry

```go
type DispatcherEntry struct {

#### func (DispatcherEntry) Validate

```go
func (e DispatcherEntry) Validate() error
```

Validate checks the entry as the write hooks do: 0 (unused) is valid; otherwise the producer must be a node-ID 1..127 (a SAM producer sends its own node-ID), neither index may be 0, and both blocks must end at sub-index FFh at the latest. A refusal is [canopen.AbortInvalidValue](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortInvalidValue).

### type Producer

```go
type Producer struct {

	// serialises transmissions

}
```

Producer is an MPDO producer: TPDO n of a dictionary whose mapping sub-index 00h is 0xFE (SAM) or 0xFF (DAM). It reads the COB-ID, transmission type and inhibit time at every transmission, so it follows changes of the parameters. Transmissions are serialised and respect the inhibit time: a transmission that comes too early waits (Lely refuses it with EAGAIN instead). The producer has no goroutine.

#### func NewProducer

```go
func NewProducer(bus canopen.Bus, d *od.Dictionary, n int, opts ...Option) (*Producer, error)
```

NewProducer returns the MPDO producer of TPDO n (1..512) of d. It installs the MPDO reconfiguration rules ([ProtectPDO](#func-protectpdo)) and does nothing on the bus. Call Start, and SetEnabled(true) when the node is NMT operational.

#### func (Producer) Send

```go
func (p *Producer) Send(ctx context.Context, index uint16, sub uint8) error
```

Send sends a SAM-MPDO of the local object index:sub. The TPDO must be a SAM producer (mapping sub 00h 0xFE), the dictionary's node-ID valid, and the object listed in an object scanner list (ErrNotScanned), existing ([canopen.AbortNoObject](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortNoObject), [canopen.AbortNoSubIndex](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortNoSubIndex)), PDO-mappable and readable ([canopen.AbortNotMappable](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortNotMappable)), and at most 4 bytes long ([canopen.AbortPDOLength](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortPDOLength)); it is read with a remote read, so read hooks apply.

#### func (Producer) SendDAM

```go
func (p *Producer) SendDAM(ctx context.Context, dest canopen.NodeID, index uint16, sub uint8, value []byte) error
```

SendDAM sends a DAM-MPDO: value (at most 4 bytes, padded with zeros) for object index:sub of node dest, or of every consumer when dest is 0. The TPDO must be a DAM producer (mapping sub 00h 0xFF). A value longer than 4 bytes fails with [canopen.AbortPDOLength](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortPDOLength), dest above 127 with [canopen.ErrInvalidNodeID](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#ErrInvalidNodeID).
